title: O Lord, Thy Perfect Word
description: O Lord, Thy Perfect Word in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 191 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Superiority of the Scriptures”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord, thy per-fect word Di-rects our steps a-right; Nor can all oth-er books af-ford Such prof-it or de-light.

lines: Nor can all other books afford
To distant lands its glory spreads,
O, may we hide it in our hearts,

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
